title: Committee of Supply – Head O (Ministry of Health)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head O (Ministry of Health)

sections.label: Remaking medical system foundations
sections.summary: The passage states that recent years saw a remaking of the medical system's foundations through the Pioneer Generation Package, MediShield Life, CHAS, MediSave flexibility and increased subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The past few years have been marked by a remarkable remaking of the foundations of our medical system – the Pioneer Generation Package, MediShield Life, a rejuvenated and expanded CHAS programme, increased flexibility of MediSave usage and increased subsidies across the board for all manner of medical services.

sections.label: Rising obesity and diabetes reports
sections.summary: The passage states two reports: rising obesity rates in Singapore, especially among children, and Singapore having the second highest diabetes prevalence among developed nations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Two worrying reports have recently surfaced: the first is that obesity rates in Singapore are rising and, in particular, amongst our children; the second, unsurprisingly given the first report, is that Singapore has the second highest prevalence of diabetes amongst developed nations.

sections.label: Incentives for healthy lifestyle adherence
sections.summary: The passage states that Singaporeans in approved wellness programmes or with healthy lifestyles could get tax rebates or discounted public healthcare rates, and chronic disease patients adhering to treatment could get extra credit.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Page: 126 Singaporeans who participate regularly in approved wellness programmes or can demonstrate that they adhere to a healthy lifestyle with regular exercise, for instance, could receive tax rebates or pay discounted rates at public healthcare institutions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Similarly, patients with chronic diseases who adhere to their treatment programmes and clinical pathways could receive extra credit for their medical expenses.

sections.label: Community Health Networks for Seniors
sections.summary: The passage states the speaker is heartened by the announcement of Community Health Networks for Seniors and hopes the Ministry can shed more light on the initiative.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: For the elderly, I am heartened by the announcement of the setting up of Community Health Networks for Seniors and I hope the Ministry can shed more light on this initiative.

sections.label: Expanding Intermediate and Long-term Care
sections.summary: The passage states the speaker welcomes Ministry moves to expand Intermediate and Long-term Care capacity and capability under the Healthcare Masterplan and is encouraged by Action Plan for Successful Ageing principles.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: For seniors, the ravages of age alone can lead to increasing dependence.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I welcome the moves made by the Ministry to expand the capacity and capability of our Intermediate and Long-term Care sector under the Healthcare Masterplan and am encouraged by the principles that have been embodied in the Action Plan for Successful Ageing.

sections.label: Queenstown super-aged community statistics
sections.summary: The passage states Queenstown is classified as super-aged, with over one in five residents over 65, and cites a Straits Times article on households of residents 65 or older living alone.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: My ward of Queenstown is already what would be classified as a super-aged community, the definition of which is that over one in five residents are over 65 years of age.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: A recent article in The Straits Times noted that there were 41,200 households made up of residents aged 65 or older who live alone and that this number was expected to rise to 83,000 by 2030.

sections.label: Singapore Quality of Death Index
sections.summary: Singapore ranked 12th in the Economist Intelligence Unit's Quality of Death Index last year despite being ranked among the world's healthiest countries.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Despite being ranked as one of the healthiest countries in the world and one of the best places to be born in, Singapore was only ranked 12th in the Quality of Death Index released by the Economist Intelligence Unit last year.

sections.label: Polyclinic waiting time KPI
sections.summary: The 2016 Budget Book set a polyclinic waiting time KPI of a maximum of 100 minutes, and over 95% of cases met it for the last few years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: What else is the Ministry doing to ensure sustainability of our healthcare system as we hit from SG51 towards SG100?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In the 2016 Budget Book, the KPI for polyclinic waiting time was set at a maximum of 100 minutes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: By this standard, over 95% of cases consistently met the KPI for the last few years.

sections.label: Polyclinic waiting times 2016
sections.summary: In February 2016, median registration and consultation waiting time was about half an hour, but the 95th percentile was closer to two hours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In February 2016, total waiting time for registration plus consultation was roughly half an hour for the median, which is not bad, but closer to a shocking two hours for the 95th percentile.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It was two hours and 16 minutes for the 95th percentile at Bedok Polyclinic, for example.

sections.label: Long waits for specialist care
sections.summary: Three years have passed without improvement, and a patient reported waiting six months to see a lung specialist and three months for biopsy results.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, three years have passed and the situation does not seem to have improved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I have received feedback from a patient who needed to wait for six months to see a lung specialist and another three months for the biopsy result.

sections.label: SOC waiting times and referrals
sections.summary: The passage asks whether long SOC waiting times regulate subsidised patients' demand or reflect insufficient resources, and notes two ways to upgrade outpatient status.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Are these long waiting times the way SOCs regulate subsidised patients' demands for their services or are they due to insufficient resources being made available to meet subsidised patients' demands?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I understand that, currently, there are two ways for patients to upgrade their outpatient status from private tertiary care to being patients in public care at SOCs at the restructured hospitals.

sections.label: Two consecutive referral letters
sections.summary: The passage asks what the basis is for requiring two consecutive referral letters from doctors at both the SOC and the polyclinic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: What is the basis for requiring two consecutive referral letters from doctors both at the SOC and at the polyclinic?

sections.label: Downgrading private to public care
sections.summary: MOH is asked whether patients may downgrade from private to public tertiary care without a medical social worker or polyclinic referral.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Will MOH consider allowing patients to downgrade from private to public tertiary care to avoid having to seek a medical social worker to recommend the downgrade, or to skip the step of obtaining a polyclinic referral if patients are willing to go to the back of the queue and having their appointments pushed back to the end of the doctor's appointment schedule?

sections.label: Overseas Singaporeans compulsory coverage fairness
sections.summary: The scheme benefits those based in Singapore, but requiring all overseas Singaporeans to pay for compulsory coverage seems unfair to some and merits review.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: While the scheme benefits those of us based here, requiring all overseas Singaporeans to pay for compulsory coverage does not seem fair to some of them and merits a review.

sections.label: Overseas Singaporeans opt out and premiums
sections.summary: The Government is asked to review letting overseas Singaporeans opt out, as MediShield Life premiums rise while subsidies are reduced from this year to 2019.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Will the Government review how it could allow such overseas Singaporeans to opt out of the scheme?

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In fact, rising MediShield Life premiums will be a reality for many Singaporeans as the subsidy threshold is progressively reduced from this year up to the year 2019, when MediShield Life subsidies come to an end.

sections.label: Moratorium ending and higher premiums
sections.summary: The moratorium lasts only until November this year, so the prospects of higher premiums next year are asked about.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As this moratorium will only last until November this year, what are the prospects of higher premiums next year?

sections.label: Screening and abnormal results detected
sections.summary: About 60% had never attended any screening before, and 60% with no past history were detected with abnormal results.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: About 60% of them had never attended any screening before and 60% of them, who had no past history, were detected with abnormal results.

sections.label: Diabetics with poor control
sections.summary: Presently, one in three diabetics has poor control of their diabetes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Presently, one in three diabetics has poor control of their diabetes.

sections.label: Calorie content disclosure proposal
sections.summary: A speaker asks whether MOH would consider promoting less-calorie food intake, such as disclosing calorie content in available food.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: An area that can make a difference is to enhance lifestyle-change reinforcements.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Thus, would MOH consider promoting less-calorie food intake within our population, such as disclosure of calorie content in the food available?

sections.label: Home and community care plans
sections.summary: A speaker asks MOH for updates on home-care and community care plans, caregiver support, and holistic care near or at home.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Can MOH give an update on our home-care and community care plans?

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Can MOH tell us how we can further empower and support caregivers?

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: And can MOH advise us on how we can ensure care can be delivered near to home – or even at home – in a holistic, integrated, sustainable way so that we can look after all our Singaporean patients, those who are mobile, those less mobile and those who are unable to leave the home easily?

sections.label: Action Plan for Successful Ageing
sections.summary: The Action Plan for Successful Ageing includes about 60 initiatives covering 12 areas.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The Action Plan for Successful Ageing includes about 60 initiatives covering 12 areas.

sections.label: National Seniors' Health Programme
sections.summary: The National Seniors' Health Programme is one of the initiatives of the Action Plan for Successful Ageing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
sentences.text: One of the initiatives of the Action Plan for Successful Ageing is the National Seniors' Health Programme.

sections.label: Promoting seniors' healthy living
sections.summary: A speaker asks the Minister to share plans for promoting and supporting seniors to keep healthy, so active living is not seen as only for the young and fit.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: We must also ensure that seniors do not think that active living is only for the young and fit.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Therefore, I would like to ask the Minister to share and update what is his plan in promoting and supporting seniors to keep healthy.

sections.label: Community Networks for Seniors
sections.summary: A speaker says everyone must do their part and sees Community Networks for Seniors as critical to keeping seniors plugged into social and support networks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Every one of us has to do our part.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: I see the Community Networks for Seniors being critical in this aspect, as they have the potential to ensure our seniors continue to be plugged in to social and support networks.

sections.label: Elderly care and lifespan
sections.summary: It asks whether the Community Networks for Seniors can simplify assistance and distribute resources fairly, and notes Singaporeans born in 2014 have an average lifespan of 82.8 years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Perhaps, this initiative can be akin to the Pioneer Generation Ambassador (PGA) programme in which volunteers are empowered through proper training and given a modest honorarium.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Thirdly, can the Community Networks for Seniors help to simplify the process of delivering assistance and care to our elderly, so that the elderly only need to approach one touch point?

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: The coordinating nature of the Community Networks for Seniors can also ensure that resources and support are fairly distributed to all seniors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: The average lifespan of Singaporeans born in 2014 is now 82.8 years, 7.5 years longer than in 1990.

sections.label: Adult smoking proportion fall
sections.summary: The proportion of adult smokers fell from 18.3% to 13.3% over the last 20 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: The proportion of adult smokers fell from 18.3% to 13.3% over the last 20 years.

sections.label: New hospitals and beds
sections.summary: In 2015, three new acute and community hospitals were opened progressively and over 900 beds were added.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: In 2015 alone, we opened three new acute and community hospitals progressively and added over 900 beds − Ng Teng Fong General Hospital and Jurong Community Hospital in the West, and Yishun Community Hospital in the North.

sections.label: Subsidised appointment wait times
sections.summary: Median wait times for subsidised new appointments stayed at about 29 days over three years, while 95th percentile wait times rose from 110 to 125 days.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Despite the increasing workload, the median wait times for subsidised new appointments remained fairly constant, at about 29 days over the past three years, while the 95th percentile wait times increased from 110 to 125 days.

sections.label: Consultation wait times improved
sections.summary: Median consultation wait times improved from 32 minutes in 2011 to around 14 minutes in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Median consultation wait times have improved from 32 minutes in 2011 to around 14 minutes in 2015.

sections.label: Polyclinic redevelopment and workforce growth
sections.summary: Polyclinics are being redeveloped and new ones are on track by 2020, while the healthcare professional workforce grew 24% from 46,000 to 57,000 between 2011 and 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Currently, we are redeveloping Bedok, Ang Mo Kio and Yishun Polyclinics and are on track to open new polyclinics in Jurong West, Punggol and Bukit Panjang, and a new primary care facility in Sembawang by 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: To meet the increasing healthcare demand, we have grown the healthcare professional workforce of doctors, nurses, pharmacists and allied health professionals by 24% from 46,000 to 57,000 between 2011 and 2015.

sections.label: Singaporeans receiving enhanced subsidies
sections.summary: As of December 2015, 715,000 Singaporeans had benefited from these enhanced subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: As of December 2015, 715,000 Singaporeans have benefited from these enhanced subsidies.

sections.label: MediShield Life claims and increase
sections.summary: From last December to February, MediShield Life approved about $136 million for 95,000 claims, a 29% increase over 2015 monthly average.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Overall, from last December to February this year, MediShield Life approved about $136 million for 95,000 claims, or about $45.3 million per month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: This is a 29% increase, compared to the average monthly claim for MediShield in 2015.

sections.label: Shift to community-based care
sections.summary: The healthcare delivery system is being transformed from hospital-centric to community-based care meeting Singaporeans' needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Beyond hospital-centric to community-based care, we are transforming our healthcare delivery system from one that is built around the hospital, to one that is directed at meeting the needs of Singaporeans.

sections.label: Building care sectors and networks
sections.summary: Building up primary, intermediate, long-term and home-care sectors and hospital networks has streamlined processes, enabled shorter stays and faster recovery.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Over the last few years, we have done this by building up the primary, intermediate, long-term and home-care sectors, and the networks between hospitals and these care partners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: These have helped to streamline processes, enable shorter hospital stays and support faster recovery for patients.

sections.label: RHS care pathway workflow
sections.summary: The pathway organises RHS care providers into a coherent workflow, allowing timely surgery, shorter acute stays and faster rehabilitation transition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: The pathway organises the different care providers in the RHS into a coherent workflow to efficiently care for the patients, allowing for a more timely surgery, shorter acute hospital stays, and faster transition to rehabilitation at St Andrew's Community Hospital next door.

sections.label: Doubling of healthcare budget
sections.summary: The healthcare budget more than doubled from $4.7 billion in FY2012 to $11 billion this year, partly due to ageing, infrastructure and greater government cost share.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Our healthcare budget has more than doubled from $4.7 billion in financial year (FY) 2012 to $11 billion this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: This has come about partly because of ageing and the need to invest in infrastructure, but also because of the Government's policy shift to take on a greater proportion of healthcare costs.

sections.label: Agency for Care Effectiveness
sections.summary: Singapore set up the Agency for Care Effectiveness to evaluate clinical and cost effectiveness of health technologies and guide their proper use.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: As part of the "Choosing Wisely" campaign, medical bodies in the United States (US), Canada, the United Kingdom (UK), Australia and Japan have identified 400 areas of unnecessary or low value tests and treatments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We, too, have recently set up the Agency for Care Effectiveness (ACE) to expand our capacity in evaluating the clinical and cost effectiveness of health technologies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: ACE will look into high-cost treatments and technologies, systematically evaluate and develop guidance to guide the proper use of such treatments and technology, and encourage providers to manage costs while providing quality care.

sections.label: Global and Singapore diabetes numbers
sections.summary: WHO reported global adults with diabetes quadrupled since 1980 to over 400 million in 2014, with over 400,000 in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: The World Health Organization (WHO) recently announced that the global number of adults living with diabetes has quadrupled since 1980 to over 400 million in 2014; and of this 400 million, over 400,000 are in Singapore – they are Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Among Singaporeans, about 400,000 have diabetes, and one in three Singaporeans has a lifetime risk to develop diabetes; 30% lifetime risk.

sections.label: Diabetes economic burden study
sections.summary: A Saw Swee Hock School of Public Health study estimated diabetes costs working-age adults more than $1 billion a year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: A Saw Swee Hock School of Public Health study estimated the total economic burden of diabetes for working-age adults at more than $1 billion a year.

sections.label: US pre-diabetes lifestyle study
sections.summary: A US study found pre-diabetics reduced diabetes incidence by 58% through diet, exercise and behaviour modification, and by up to 71% for those aged 60 and older.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: In a US study published in the New England Journal of Medicine, pre-diabetics can reduce the overall incidence of diabetes by 58% through diet, exercise and behaviour modification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: That is why I said we still have hope.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: These lifestyle changes worked particularly well for participants aged 60 and older, reducing their risk by up to 71%.

sections.label: Singaporeans lifetime diabetes risk
sections.summary: Singaporeans have a one-third possibility of contracting diabetes during their lifetime.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Our Singaporeans have a one-third possibility of contracting diabetes during their lifetime.

sections.label: Diabetes Prevention and Care Taskforce
sections.summary: A Diabetes Prevention and Care Taskforce will develop a multi-year action plan, mobilise the nation and monitor outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: To coordinate the strategies on the war on diabetes, I will be co-chairing a Diabetes Prevention and Care Taskforce together with Mr Ng Chee Meng, Acting Minister for Education.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: The task force will include representatives from Government agencies, private sector, patient advocacy and caregiver groups and will: (a) develop and implement a multi-year action plan for the war on diabetes; (b) reach out and mobilise the nation to fight the disease together; and (c) monitor and evaluate the outcomes of our efforts.

sections.label: Mental health definition and community care
sections.summary: It defines good mental health and states community mental healthcare is almost non-existent, with undiagnosed and under-treated patients.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo
sentences.text: Good or normal mental health is a state of well-being in which the individual, amongst other things, can realise his or her own abilities, can cope with the normal stresses of life, can work productively and is able to function normally in the community.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo
sentences.text: This is especially urgent for community mental healthcare which is almost non-existent.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo
sentences.text: There is a problem of undiagnosed and under-treated mental patients in the community.

sections.label: Psychiatric staff at Social Service Offices
sections.summary: It asks whether MOH can place psychiatric nurse practitioners or psychologists at Social Service Offices to diagnose and refer undiagnosed mental patients.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo
sentences.text: Is it possible for MOH to maintain a staff of psychiatric nurse practitioners or psychologists at Social Service Offices (SSOs) to diagnose and refer undiagnosed mental patients for follow-up?

sections.label: Outpatient commitment law consideration
sections.summary: It asks whether MOH will consider an outpatient commitment law like Kendra's Law, allowing community living under close monitoring.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo
sentences.text: Will MOH consider an "outpatient commitment" law, similar to Kendras' Law in the US, where there is some restrictive form of commitment for a mentally ill individual, whereby the individual is free to live in the community, provided he is subject to close monitoring by a physician or agency?

sections.label: De-stigmatising mental health
sections.summary: It states animosity hinders sufferers and families from seeking help, and asks what the Ministry plans to de-stigmatise mental health.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: The animosity, in turn, makes it more difficult for those suffering from these conditions or even their family members to consider the issue and seek professional help.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: Therefore, I would like to ask the Minister, looking ahead, what does the Ministry plan to do to de-stigmatise mental health?

sections.label: Mental health prevalence and insurance limits
sections.summary: It cites studies estimating one in six suffer mental health issues, and notes MediSave and MediShield Life psychiatric coverage limits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Some studies estimate that one in six of our population would suffer from mental health issues at some stage of their lives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, MediSave has a withdrawal limit of $150 per day for inpatient psychiatric treatment, with an annual cap of $5,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For MediShield Life, the difference is even greater, with a daily coverage of $700 in a normal ward, but $100 for a psychiatric ward.

sections.label: Singapore dementia preparedness
sections.summary: It asks how prepared Singapore is for rising dementia patients, citing an estimate that 10% above 60 have dementia.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Another equally important issue is how prepared is Singapore to deal with the rising numbers of patients with dementia.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It was recently estimated that 10% of us aged above 60 suffer from dementia, with a rise in younger patients being diagnosed.

sections.label: Projected number increase 2012 to 2030
sections.summary: The number is projected to rise from 28,000 in 2012 to 80,000 in 2030.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: The number is projected to increase from 28,000 in 2012 to 80,000 in 2030.

sections.label: Inactive nurses and community nursing core
sections.summary: Over 5,700 registered and enrolled nurses were inactive in 2014, and the Ministry is asked to consider a community nursing core.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: First, there were over 5,700 registered and enrolled nurses who were not active in 2014, comprising over 15% of the total number of nurses.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This is an existing pool of qualified nurses that can be tapped on if appropriate flexibility, allowances and incentives are given to encourage them to provide home-based healthcare within their neighbourhoods and communities.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I ask the Ministry to consider developing a community nursing core to attract retired, inactive or underemployed nurses to return to active nursing and to cater to existing active nurses who need job flexibility due to family or other reasons, so that they do not leave active nursing.

sections.label: Certified courses and pilot homecare model
sections.summary: Carers are certified at course end, and one pilot homecare model is supported by MOH and funded by Temasek.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo
sentences.text: They are certified at the end of their courses, which teach them skills like assisted feeding, catheter care, prosthesis use, simple dressings and simple grooming, as in toenail cutting for non-diabetics using sterile techniques.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo
sentences.text: There is one pilot homecare model in my constituency supported by MOH and funded by Temasek called Ageing Gracefully At Home.

sections.label: Befrienders watching weak senior residents
sections.summary: Healthier seniors are reimbursed as befrienders to watch and report weak residents to Seniors Activity Centres.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo
sentences.text: Some of the healthier senior neighbours are recruited and reimbursed as befrienders to keep watch, befriend and report on weak and sick residents in their charge to the Seniors Activity Centres (SACs) downstairs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo
sentences.text: I find this scheme useful as it keeps the residents in their own homes for as long as possible, without which, many of them would have invariably ended up in acute hospitals.

sections.label: Eldercare centres, staffing and dementia demand
sections.summary: The Minister is asked about enough eldercare centres, hospitals and hospices, and about recruiting and retaining carers and therapists.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
sentences.text: With reference to this scenario, I would like to ask the Minister and the Ministry if we will have enough eldercare centres, step-down community hospitals and hospices to cope with an increasing number of seniors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
sentences.text: How will we recruit, train and retain enough volunteer carers, volunteer guides, nurses, nursing assistants, professional caregivers and therapists?

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: Also, the incidence of dementia will rise, too, making care for our elderly even more challenging as this requires certain care specialisation and adjustments in the communities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: Hence, could the Ministry share the projected demand for eldercare services and facilities, such as day rehabilitation centres, dementia day care centres and home-care?

sections.label: Right siting and hospice care subsidies
sections.summary: This is right siting compared to acute hospital bed occupancy, and MOH is asked to review hospice care subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo
sentences.text: This is also right siting, compared to occupancy of acute hospital beds by such patients.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo
sentences.text: Thus, could MOH review the subsidies for hospice care?

sections.label: Palliative care staffing shortage
sections.summary: Palliative care aims to add life to patients' days, and the shortage of palliative care doctors, nurses and social workers will worsen with an ageing population.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo
sentences.text: The purpose of palliative care is to make life more comfortable for these patients by adding life to their days.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo
sentences.text: There is an urgent need to expand the number of palliative care doctors, nurses and social workers, as the shortage now will be even more pronounced in years to come with our ageing population.

sections.label: Hospice subsidies and income ceiling
sections.summary: The speaker urges MOH to reduce hospice care costs, asks how many benefited from the last income ceiling increase, and proposes raising it and extending ElderShield.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo
sentences.text: Therefore, I urge MOH to consider ways to reduce the burden of patients of hospice care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: I understand that patients whose families have a per capita monthly household income of $2,601 and above will not receive any subsidies for inpatient hospice care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: With one in four Singaporeans estimated to be over 60 by 2030, the demand for such specialised care will increase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: How many people have benefited so far from the last increase in the income ceiling?

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: In light of the gradual increase in gross monthly income and the increase in cost of living, I would like to know if the Ministry is considering raising the income ceiling so as to allow more families to benefit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: I would also like to propose that ElderShield be extended for the use of hospice and palliative care.

sections.label: Palliative care use and training
sections.summary: Singapore ranks 12th in the 2015 Quality of Death Index, over 10,000 people yearly will need palliative care by 2020, and many doctors and nurses report inadequate training.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to the 2015 Quality of Death Index, Singapore is the 12th best place in the world to die.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: By 2020, more than 10,000 people a year here are expected to need palliative care.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Only about 20% to 30% of those who pass away each year use palliative care services when research shows that up to 70% to 80% of all deaths might have actually benefited from such care.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A Lien Foundation survey showed that six in 10 doctors and four in 10 nurses said their basic training did not prepare them to handle patients with life-threatening illnesses.

sections.label: Caregiver mental illness risk
sections.summary: An OECD 2011 report found long-term caregivers were 20% more likely than non-caregivers to suffer mental illness.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Organisation of Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) 2011 report found that long-term caregivers were 20% more likely than non-caregivers to suffer mental illness.

sections.label: Nursing taskforce and progressive wages
sections.summary: The 2012 National Nursing Taskforce strengthened nursing careers, and the speaker wants MOH to coordinate a Progressive Wage/Career Model for Admin, Ancillary and Allied Health workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2012, the National Nursing Taskforce (NNT) was set up by MOH to look into strengthening the development of the nursing profession to better meet the population's healthcare needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This helped to push for better career progression for the nurses and helped overcome many issues.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We acknowledge that the review of non-nursing staff group, Admin, Ancillary and Allied Health, is currently ongoing at the various cluster levels and would like MOH to play a larger role in the coordination and implementation of Progressive Wage/Career Model for the Admin, Ancillary and Allied Health Workers across the healthcare clusters in the public healthcare sector.

sections.label: ILTC career pathways and income
sections.summary: Some locals who switched to the ILTC sector found meaning in their work but left because income and career pathways were less clearly defined than in mainstream hospitals.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Through our interactions with healthcare workers in the ILTC sector, we know that there are locals who have switched careers to the ILTC sector and found meaning in their work.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, as their income and career pathways are not as clearly defined compared to those in the mainstream hospitals, some have struggled to sustain with these incomes and eventually left the industry.

sections.label: Work-Life Grant for FWAs
sections.summary: The Government introduced the Work-Life Grant to provide funding and incentives for companies to promote FWAs.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To promote FWAs, the Government introduced the Work-Life Grant which provides funding and incentives for companies.

sections.label: Chronic Disease Management Programme
sections.summary: The Chronic Disease Management Programme was first introduced in October 2006 to reduce out-of-pocket cash payment for outpatient bills.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Chronic Disease Management Programme was first introduced in October 2006 to reduce out-of-pocket cash payment for outpatient bills.

sections.label: Medical manpower and staffing demand
sections.summary: The passage asks if there are plans to study these models further, notes three medical schools and training duration, and cites ongoing staffing demand and manpower deficits.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With reference to this, I would like to ask the Minister if there are plans to study further on these models.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
sentences.text: We have also now got three medical schools, but the output of doctors will, of course, take time due to training duration.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
sentences.text: In the various sectors, such as acute and ILTC care, there is an ongoing demand for staffing.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
sentences.text: I would also go on to say that we have manpower deficits in many departments across many disciplines.

sections.label: MOH manpower competition plans
sections.summary: The passage asks what plans and framework MOH has for manpower competition from the same central pool, and notes the National Nursing Taskforce's recommendations were accepted.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
sentences.text: With the newer institutions being built and the opening of their doors, the manpower competition is from the same central pool and, thus, it is the same warm bodies that we are competing for.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
sentences.text: What plans and framework does MOH have to handle this manpower situation?

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: We all know that our nurses play an essential role in the ILTC sector and the National Nursing Taskforce's recommendations for the future of the nursing profession have already been accepted by the Ministry.

sections.label: Protecting nurses from abuse
sections.summary: The passage asks what the Ministry will do to protect nurses from abuse by patients and family members, citing a report estimating about seven in 10 healthcare workers suffered such abuse.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In addition, what will the Ministry do to protect our nurses from abuse from patients and their family members?

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: This comes about because there was a worrying report in the Annals of the Academy of Medicine that estimated that about seven in 10 of our healthcare workers have suffered from such abuse.

sections.label: Workplace health screening for seniors
sections.summary: MOH and HPB are bringing health screening and health education to the workplace and customising programmes for seniors in different work environments to extend their longevity in the workforce.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: In order to further extend their longevity in the workforce, MOH and the Health Promotion Board (HPB) are bringing health screening and health education to the workplace and going "deeper" by customising the programmes for seniors working in different work environments.

sections.label: Bus captains health screening results
sections.summary: About half of bus captains with abnormal screening results improved in at least one area at a second screening about eight months later, and about half of these reached normal status in all aspects.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Almost half of the bus captains with abnormal screening results initially showed at least one improvement, either in their blood pressure, blood glucose or cholesterol at their second health screening which was about eight months after the first one.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: And of these, about half achieved normal health status in all aspects of their health screening.

sections.label: Reaching mature workers and seniors
sections.summary: The target is to reach 120,000 mature workers in seven sectors by 2025, and seniors' health education is promoted via the People's Association's Wellness Programme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Our target is to reach out to 120,000 mature workers in seven sectors by 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: In the community, we are systematically promoting seniors' health education via the People's Association's (PA's) Wellness Programme.

sections.label: Mobile preventive health services for seniors
sections.summary: MOH partners organisations to bring preventive health services to seniors, including retrofitted Hearing Buses and a Paya Lebar Wellness Centre with weekly health monitoring by retired volunteer nurses.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: In addition, MOH partners organisations to bring preventive health services to the doorstep of our seniors.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: We are experimenting with putting health checks, vaccination, dental, eye and foot checks and even hearing tests on wheels so that they can come to locations closer to our seniors in the community.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: The National University Health System has thus retrofitted two Hearing Buses to bring audio checks to different neighbourhoods instead.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: This mobile Hearing Bus has started its journey of screening hearing for our seniors in Yuhua, Bukit Panjang, Nee Soon Central, Whampoa and Tampines West as a pilot and we will see how that goes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: PA has worked with The Goodlife Cooperative (TGLC) in Paya Lebar to integrate preventive health services with social outreach and wellness programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Seniors can access basic health monitoring services weekly at the Paya Lebar Wellness Centre where retired volunteer nurses provide health advice and help seniors take their blood pressure, monitoring their blood glucose level, their height and weight measurements.

sections.label: Preventing diabetes in pregnant women
sections.summary: Women, especially pregnant women, need help preventing diabetes because children of mothers with gestational diabetes mellitus are at higher risk of obesity and diabetes later in life.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: Hence, we need to actively help women, especially pregnant women, prevent diabetes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: This is because many children of mothers who had gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) while pregnant are at higher risk of suffering obesity and diabetes later on in life.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: Therefore, whether it is for the well-being of women or our young, we must step up our efforts to actively manage and prevent diabetes.

sections.label: Integrated women's health screening package
sections.summary: A more integrated package for women's health screening is to be offered at subsidised rates, with more publicity as well.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
sentences.text: First, a more integrated package for women's health screening at subsidised rates and more publicity as well.

sections.label: Clementi polyclinic chronic disease patients
sections.summary: The Clementi polyclinic's headcount of chronic disease patients rose from 32,600 in 2012 to just over 35,070 in 2015, a 7% increase in three years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: We already see this in Clementi where I serve: the Clementi polyclinic is very busy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: I was informed that their headcount of chronic disease patients has increased: 32,600 in 2012; just over 35,070 in 2015; a 7% increase in three years.

sections.label: Polyclinic space in mature estates
sections.summary: MOH must work with other agencies to set aside space for polyclinic expansion in mature housing estates.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: As such, it will be important for MOH to work together with other agencies to set aside space for polyclinic expansion in our mature housing estates.

sections.label: CHAS income cap raise
sections.summary: The monthly household income per member cap for CHAS subsidies should be raised from $1,800 to $3,900, the 2015 median monthly income from work.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
sentences.text: The monthly household income per member capped to qualify for CHAS subsidies should be raised from $1,800 to the prevailing median monthly income from work for an individual which stands at $3,900 in 2015.

sections.label: Busy eastern polyclinics
sections.summary: Eastern polyclinics such as Bedok, Geylang East and Marine Parade are very busy, and it is asked whether MOH can consider another polyclinic in the Geylang, Eunos, Haig Road and Ubi vicinity.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
sentences.text: For example, in the eastern part of Singapore, the polyclinics are very heavy in terms of patient load.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
sentences.text: Bedok, Geylang East and the newly renovated and opened Marine Parade polyclinics are all very busy clinics, besides the Clementi one that I just heard about.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
sentences.text: Some seniors tell me they have to place an item or stand in line from as early as 6.30 in the morning.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
sentences.text: Can MOH consider having another polyclinic in the Geylang, Eunos, Haig Road and Ubi vicinity to meet the needs of the patients there?

sections.label: National Silver Academy courses
sections.summary: The National Silver Academy, a network of education institutions and VWOs, will offer over 10,000 learning places across 500 courses this year, with registration from next month for those aged 50 and above.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: The Academy is not a physical campus, but made up of a network of education institutions and VWOs offering courses in various fields to seniors.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: I am pleased to announce that the National Silver Academy will offer over 10,000 learning places across 500 courses this year and that seniors aged 50 and above can start to register for courses from next month onwards.

sections.label: Course fee subsidy for seniors
sections.summary: Singaporeans aged 50 and above will receive a subsidy of up to 50% off the course fee under the Academy.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Under the Academy, Singaporeans aged 50 and above will receive a subsidy of up to 50% off the course fee.

sections.label: Home and community care capacity
sections.summary: Home and community care capacities have expanded to 6,900 home-care and 3,500 day care places, with a target of 10,000 home care and 6,200 day care places by 2020, plus Guidelines for Home and Centre-based Care introduced last year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: In the past five years, as my Minister has noted earlier, we have expanded home and community care capacities to 6,900 home-care places and 3,500 day care places today.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: We will continue to work hard to develop more infrastructure and manpower needed to grow our services and we are on track to meet the projected demand of 10,000 home care and 6,200 day care places by 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: I agree with Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef that beyond capacity, we need to continually enhance the quality of care.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: We introduced the Guidelines for Home and Centre-based Care last year and are committed to supporting providers in working towards these Guidelines.

sections.label: Home and Community Care Masterplan
sections.summary: MOH will pilot new initiatives under a new Home and Community Care Masterplan this year to help seniors age at home.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: MOH will pilot a number of new initiatives under a new Home and Community Care Masterplan this year to better support seniors to age at home.

sections.label: Eldercarer pilot for domestic helpers
sections.summary: MOH will launch an "Eldercarer" pilot giving domestic helpers comprehensive training before deployment to families' homes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: MOH will launch a new "Eldercarer" pilot to provide comprehensive training to domestic helpers before they are deployed to the families' homes.

sections.label: Befriending movement growth target
sections.summary: The Action Plan for Successful Ageing targets growing the befriending movement to 50 communities by 2020, over 1,000 befrienders and some 3,000 befriendees.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Our target under the Action Plan for Successful Ageing is to grow the befriending movement to 50 communities by 2020, which means more than 1,000 befrienders and some 3,000 befriendees.

sections.label: Eldercare packages pilot capacity
sections.summary: Some three eldercare providers will offer these packages with a capacity of over 300 places in the pilot phase.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Some three eldercare providers will be offering these packages with a capacity of over 300 places in the pilot phase.

sections.label: AAHs in future HDB developments
sections.summary: At least 10 future HDB housing developments will have these AAHs by 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: At least 10 future HDB housing developments will have these AAHs by 2020.

sections.label: Integrated Operator scheme pilot
sections.summary: MOH will pilot an Integrated Operator scheme this year, launching RFPs for bundles of nursing homes, eldercare centres and home-care.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: To give integration of care a bigger push, MOH will pilot a new Integrated Operator (IOP) scheme this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: MOH will launch Request for Proposals (RFPs) to appoint operators for bundles of "three-in-one" care facilities and services, comprising nursing homes, eldercare centres and home-care, within the same area.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Under this new IOP scheme, the sector may see up to 500 nursing home beds, 240 day care places and 150 home-care places, within one tender.

sections.label: Workforce development and South region RFP
sections.summary: They are expected to train and build manpower capabilities, starting with an RFP for one South region bundle later this year, subject to market conditions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: They are also expected to do more in terms of workforce development, that is, to train and build up the manpower capabilities in this sector.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: We will start with an RFP for one bundle – for the South region – later this year, but subject to market conditions.

sections.label: Pilot recruiting neighbour carers
sections.summary: MOH wants to work with community partners to recruit and train more neighbour carers, including able and active elderly, paired with seniors living alone.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: As part of this pilot, MOH wants to work with different partners in the community to recruit and train more neighbour carers that can include the more able and active elderly, as suggested by some Members, who can be paired with the seniors living alone in the community.

sections.label: ILTC portal and recruitment
sections.summary: An online ILTC Careers Portal launched in 2013 and a branding campaign raised awareness, with 107 locals recruited through job fairs over the past year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: We launched the online ILTC Careers Portal in 2013 and a branding campaign earlier this year to raise awareness of opportunities in this sector.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: We have facilitated the recruitment of 107 locals through our job fairs over the past one year.

sections.label: Aged care training and recruitment incentives
sections.summary: Training in geriatric and palliative care was strengthened, a Community Care Placement Bonus introduced, and a Senior Management Associate Scheme launched for mid-career talents.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: We have strengthened training in areas, such as geriatric and palliative care, in a three-month refresher course and enhanced the training allowances.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: There will also be a new one-time Community Care Placement Bonus at $3,000 for Enrolled Nurses and $5,000 for Registered Nurses who join the aged care sector.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: There is also an increasing need for professionals, managers, executives and technicians (PMETs) who can take on management and supervisory positions in new aged care facilities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: We have, therefore, launched a new Senior Management Associate Scheme to attract mid-career talents with supervisory or managerial experience, who are interested to explore a career switch to the aged care sector.

sections.label: Study awards for healthcare staff
sections.summary: The $5,000 study awards will support learning in aged care, healthcare IT, analytics and healthcare system design, benefiting 50 healthcare staff this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: The $5,000 study awards will support learning and development in the areas of aged care, healthcare IT, analytics and healthcare system design, organisation and delivery, and will benefit 50 healthcare staff this year.

sections.label: NUH Basic Care Assistants pilot
sections.summary: NUH targets up to 50 Basic Care Assistants and has already hired 16 under the pilot phase.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: NUH targets to have up to 50 of such Basic Care Assistants and has already hired 16 under the pilot phase.

sections.label: AIC trains GPs for mental health
sections.summary: AIC has trained over 100 GPs and set up six specialist-led community teams to guide primary care providers managing complex mental health patients.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Second, to help detect and support the treatment of mental health patients in the community, AIC has trained and partnered over 100 GPs and set up six specialist-led community-based teams to guide our primary care providers in managing patients with more complex issues.

sections.label: Community mental health team client numbers
sections.summary: By end-2015 these teams had seen over 7,000 clients, up from 4,700 the previous year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: As at end-2015, these teams have seen over 7,000 clients, an increase from 4,700 in the previous year.

sections.label: Compulsory outpatient psychiatric treatment study
sections.summary: The Mental Health (Care and Treatment) Act does not provide for enforced outpatient psychiatric treatment; Dr Lily Neo's suggestion can be studied using overseas models.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Currently, the Mental Health (Care and Treatment) Act does not provide for enforced treatment of psychiatric patients in an outpatient setting.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: We can study Dr Lily Neo's suggestion on whether to compel outpatient mental health treatment, taking reference from overseas models, such as Scotland, England and Australia.

sections.label: Psychiatric treatment bills and subsidies
sections.summary: The 2014 median post-subsidy daily bill was $60 for psychiatric treatment versus $350 for non-psychiatric; MediShield Life and MediSave covered seven in 10 subsidised inpatient psychiatric bills.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: The median post-subsidy bill per day in 2014 was $60 for psychiatric treatment, compared to $350 for non-psychiatric treatment.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Taken together, the MediShield Life and MediSave limits were sufficient to cover seven in 10 subsidised inpatient psychiatric bills.

sections.label: Dementia support for ageing population
sections.summary: With about 10% dementia prevalence among seniors aged 60 and above, community-based support is being strengthened, including home intervention teams, CREST teams and planned day care, nursing home beds and eldercare sitters by 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: With a fast-ageing population and a dementia prevalence rate of about 10% amongst seniors aged 60 and above, we can expect the number of seniors with dementia in Singapore to grow with time.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: We are strengthening community-based support for persons with dementia and their caregivers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: We have three home intervention teams to support caregivers in managing challenging behaviours of their loved ones with dementia at home, which have reached out to close to 200 clients and caregivers to date.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: The 10 outreach CREST teams have also reached out to more than 39,000 seniors at risk islandwide.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: By 2020, we will have 3,000 dementia day care places, 1,970 dementia nursing home beds and 160 eldercare sitters.

sections.label: Gestational diabetes support for women
sections.summary: The Committee will complement the diabetes task force and look into supporting women with gestational diabetes to reduce pregnancy complications and later Type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease risk for the child.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Specifically for gestational diabetes, the Committee will complement the work of the diabetes task force and look into providing support for women with gestational diabetes to reduce the risk of complications during pregnancy and risk of Type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease for the child.

sections.label: Obese children chronic disease risk
sections.summary: Obese children are more at risk of chronic diseases and stroke later in life, but early and right intervention can prevent this.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: A major concern is that obese children are more at risk of suffering from chronic diseases and stroke later on in life.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: However, this can be prevented if intervention is done right and early.

sections.label: Child Guidance Clinics waiting times
sections.summary: In 2014, average waiting time for subsidised patients was between one week and two months, and IMH runs two Child Guidance Clinics.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
sentences.text: In 2014, the average waiting time for subsidised patients was between one week and two months." I would like to ask how are the children identified for these tests and how many of them were assessed in the last three years.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
sentences.text: IMH runs two Child Guidance Clinics located at Buangkok Green and Outram Road.

sections.label: Stigma against autism and mental health
sections.summary: Singapore's conservative society still exerts considerable social stigma on families and children with autism and other mental health issues.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
sentences.text: Our conservative society still exerts considerable social stigma to the family and children suffering from autism and other mental health issues.

sections.label: Ebola and Zika outbreaks
sections.summary: Ebola infected close to 30,000 people and claimed over 11,000 lives worldwide, while Zika affects unborn babies and can cause lifetime mental disability.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
sentences.text: Ebola cut through entire populations in West Africa and infected close to 30,000 people worldwide and claimed over 11,000 lives worldwide.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
sentences.text: Now, we face the spectre of Zika, which is not fatal but behaves in a far more sinister fashion, affecting unborn babies and potentially condemning them to a lifetime of mental disability.

sections.label: Healthcare fees transparency and inflation
sections.summary: The question asks if MOH plans to enhance healthcare fee transparency or introduce fee guidelines, noting MediShield Life coverage and private sector charges.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
sentences.text: Does MOH have any plans to enhance transparency of healthcare fees or to introduce fee guidelines to help contain healthcare inflation?

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
sentences.text: MediShield Life now provides comprehensive and universal hospitalisation coverage, but about two-thirds of Singaporeans still have integrated insurance plans (IPs) that cover them for medical services by private healthcare providers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
sentences.text: What is the Government doing to manage rising charges in the private healthcare sector?

sections.label: Chronic disease among older Singaporeans
sections.summary: One in four Singaporeans aged 40 and above has at least one chronic disease.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: One in four Singaporeans aged 40 and above has at least one chronic disease.

sections.label: Rising overweight children and youths
sections.summary: The speaker is worried that the proportion of overweight children and youths has increased over the past five years despite efforts.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Despite these efforts, it worries me that we still see the proportion of overweight children and youths increasing over the past five years.

sections.label: Students exceeding recommended screen time
sections.summary: More than 80% of surveyed students exceeded the recommended screen time of no more than two hours a day.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: More than 80% of the students surveyed exceeded the recommended screen time of no more than two hours a day.

sections.label: Myopia and dental caries in students
sections.summary: More than 60% of Primary 6 students have myopia, which may cause sight-threatening complications, and about half of Primary 1 students have dental caries.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: More than 60% of our Primary 6 students have myopia today.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: And as the condition progresses, it may result in sight-threatening complications as well.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: We have also found that about half of all our Primary 1 students have dental caries.

sections.label: NurtureSG Taskforce and Plan
sections.summary: The speaker will lead an inter-agency NurtureSG Taskforce to guide development of the NurtureSG Plan to enhance health outcomes among the young.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: To this end, I will lead an inter-agency NurtureSG Taskforce with Minister of State for Education Dr Janil Puthucheary.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: The task force comprises representatives from various Ministries, HPB, Sport Singapore and the ECDA, as well as medical professionals and academics.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: It will guide the development of the NurtureSG Plan to enhance the health outcomes among our young.

sections.label: Health promotion public consultation
sections.summary: Health promotion for the young will extend beyond school into families and the community, with a public consultation launched later this month.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Last but not least, we aim to bring health promotion for the young beyond the school and into their families and the community.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: We will launch a public consultation later this month to seek ideas on how we can encourage and enable our young to adopt and maintain healthy lifestyles.

sections.label: Psychiatric attendances for young patients
sections.summary: From 2013 to 2015 there were about 50,000 psychiatric SOC attendances for patients up to 18 years old, two-thirds seen in IMH.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: From 2013 to 2015, there were about 50,000 psychiatric SOC attendances for patients up to 18 years old, of which two-thirds were seen in IMH.

sections.label: One Singaporean One Family Doctor vision
sections.summary: The response is encapsulated in the vision "One Singaporean, One Family Doctor".

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: My response is encapsulated in our vision "One Singaporean, One Family Doctor".

sections.label: Regular family doctor benefits and uptake
sections.summary: Many positive stories illustrate benefits of a regular family doctor, but only two in five Singapore residents aged 18 to 69 have one today.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: I believe that there are many such positive stories to illustrate the benefits of having a regular family doctor.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: However, only two in five Singapore residents aged 18 to 69  have a regular family doctor today.

sections.label: CHAS subsidised care and clinic sign-ups
sections.summary: CHAS provides lower- to middle-income Singaporeans and all Pioneers subsidised care at private GP and dental clinics, with 900 GP and 650 dental clinics signed up.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Today, the CHAS provides lower- to middle-income Singaporeans and all Pioneers access to subsidised care at private GP and dental clinics, and 900 GP clinics and 650 dental clinics islandwide have signed up for CHAS.

sections.label: New polyclinics and FMCs
sections.summary: New polyclinics in Punggol and Jurong West open in 2017, another in Eunos, and two more FMCs in Tampines and Keat Hong by early 2017.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: The new polyclinics in Punggol and Jurong West will open in 2017.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: I am pleased to announce that we will build another polyclinic in Eunos, in response to Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef's query on new primary care facilities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: By early 2017, we will develop two more FMCs: one in Tampines and another one in Keat Hong.

sections.label: Total Operation Fees publication expansion
sections.summary: Total Operation Fees for common procedures in public hospitals was published in 2014 and will expand to private hospitals later this year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: In 2014, the publication of "Total Operation Fees" for common procedures in public hospitals was introduced.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: I am pleased to announce that the publication will be expanded to cover "Total Operation Fees" for private hospitals later this year.

sections.label: Three-pronged approach to external health threats
sections.summary: A three-pronged approach to external public health threats is adopted: reducing importation risk, early detection and containment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Dr Chia Shi-Lu asked about the measures that we are taking to protect Singapore against emerging diseases.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: We have adopted a three-pronged approach to external public health threats, namely, reducing the risk of importation, early detection and containment.

sections.label: GP clinics as PHPCs
sections.summary: About 640 GP clinics have volunteered as Public Health Preparedness Clinics to help manage public health emergencies such as haze and influenza pandemics.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: In the community, we work with about 640 GP clinics which have volunteered as Public Health Preparedness Clinics, or PHPCs, to help manage public health emergencies, such as haze and influenza pandemics.

sections.label: HSA dengue vaccine review
sections.summary: HSA received Sanofi's dengue vaccine regulatory filing in March 2016 and is expediting review, focusing on safety, quality and effectiveness for the local population.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: In relation to Ms Tin Pei Ling's query regarding dengue vaccination, HSA has received the regulatory filing for Sanofi's dengue vaccine in March 2016 and is expediting the review, given the dengue situation in Singapore and recognising that this is the first dengue vaccine available.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: The key focus in the Health Sciences Authority's (HSA's) review is to ensure that the vaccine is safe, of good quality and is effective for use in our local population, taking into consideration the local prevalent strains of dengue and its potential risks and adverse effects.

sections.label: Adult obesity rate rise
sections.summary: The adult obesity rate increased from 6.9% in 2004 to 10.8% in 2010.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
sentences.text: Our adult obesity rate increased from 6.9% in 2004 to 10.8% in 2010.

sections.label: Taxation on unhealthy foodstuffs
sections.summary: An unhealthy workforce is likely less efficient, affecting economic productivity, so the speaker renews a 2011 call for increased taxation on unhealthy foodstuffs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
sentences.text: And an unhealthy workforce is also likely to be less efficient, affecting our economic productivity.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
sentences.text: Hence, I would like to renew a call I first made in 2011 that the Ministry consider implementing increased taxation on unhealthy foodstuffs, such as those containing excessive fat or sugar, to discourage their consumption.

sections.label: Adult Singaporean diabetes proportion
sections.summary: Over 10% of adult Singaporeans are currently diabetic, the second highest proportion in the developed world.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
sentences.text: In fact, over 10% of adult Singaporeans are currently diabetic and it is the second highest proportion in the developed world.

sections.label: Labelling free-sugar in processed foods
sections.summary: The speaker urges focusing on empowering Singaporeans toward healthier choices and requests the Government consider mandating labelling of free-sugar content in processed foods.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
sentences.text: We should focus instead on empowering Singaporeans towards making healthier choices and adjustments to their lifestyle.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
sentences.text: I request the Government to consider mandating the labelling of free-sugar content in processed foods where the calories and percentage of daily intake of free-sugar need to be prominently displayed on food packaging.

sections.label: ElderShield long-term needs
sections.summary: ElderShield, introduced in 2002, does not adequately address the long-term needs of the severely disabled for which it was intended.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo
sentences.text: This is an important insurance scheme nowadays and will be even more so down the road in view of our ageing population.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo
sentences.text: However, in its present form, the ElderShield which was introduced in  2002 is not adequately addressing the long-term needs of the severely disabled for which it was intended.

sections.label: ElderShield cash payouts
sections.summary: Non-upgraders receive $300 for up to five years and upgraders $400 for up to six years if unable to perform three of six daily activities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo
sentences.text: Cash payouts of $300 are paid to non-upgraders for up to a maximum period of five years, and $400  are paid, for upgraders, for up to a maximum period of six years to patients who are unable to perform at least three out of six activities of daily living (ADL).

sections.label: ElderShield exclusions
sections.summary: ElderShield presently excludes those aged 70 and above in 2002 and those with existing illnesses.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo
sentences.text: Presently, ElderShield excludes those aged 70 and above in 2002 and those with existing illnesses.

sections.label: ElderShield premiums ages 60 to 64
sections.summary: For those aged 60 to 64, annual premiums to join ElderShield are from $1,000 to $3,000 respectively.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo
sentences.text: For those aged 60 to 64, the annual premiums payable to join ElderShield are from $1,000 to $3,000 respectively.

sections.label: Medical records and NEHR
sections.summary: Medical records are essential to patient care, but records across hospitals, polyclinics and GP clinics can be spread and not all are in the NEHR.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: Medical records are essential to good patient care.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: Better information means better quality diagnosis, more timely treatment and better patient safety.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: Yet, today, when patients move around across public hospitals, private hospitals, polyclinics and their local GP clinics, it can take time to get a full picture of the patients' medical records.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: Even within the same public or private hospital, information can be spread between paper and digital, sometimes in multiple digital databases, and not all databases are in the National Electronic Health Record (NEHR).

sections.label: Healthy Community Ecosystem expansion
sections.summary: The Healthy Community Ecosystem programme will be extended to nine more neighbourhoods this year, including Jalan Besar, Pasir-Ris Punggol and West Coast.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: To benefit more Singaporeans, we will be extending the Healthy Community Ecosystem programme to nine more neighbourhoods this year, including Jalan Besar, Pasir-Ris Punggol and West Coast.

sections.label: HCS market share target
sections.summary: The target is to raise total market share for HCS products to 25% by 2020, from the current 17%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Our target is to increase the total market share for HCS products to 25% by 2020, up from the current 17%.

sections.label: Lower calorie meals sold
sections.summary: Lower calorie meals sold doubled from 7.5 million in 2014 to 15 million last year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
