sentences.text: The number of lower calorie meals sold has doubled from 7.5 million in 2014 to 15 million last year.

sections.label: HPB exercise sessions doubling
sections.summary: HPB will double community and workplace exercise sessions from 100 to 200 by the end of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: To support this, HPB will double the number of exercise sessions available in the community and workplaces from the current 100 to 200 by the end of this year.

sections.label: Steps Challenge and Screen for Life
sections.summary: Mr Aidil praised the National Steps Challenge and hoped for wider extension; a second season is being prepared, and Screen for Life recommends diabetes screening for those 40 and above.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Praising the National Steps Challenge as a good initiative, Mr Aidil said he hopes this programme can be extended to more Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We are preparing for a second season of the National Steps Challenge.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Under HPB's Screen for Life programme, Singaporeans 40 and above are recommended to be screened for diabetes once every three years and, very importantly, to follow up with their family doctors after the screening.

sections.label: MOH study of suggestions
sections.summary: MOH will study these suggestions carefully as part of the ElderShield review.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: MOH will study these suggestions carefully, as part of our ElderShield review.

sections.label: ElderShield mandatory question
sections.summary: The review includes whether ElderShield should be made mandatory for every Singaporean.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Other important issues for the review include whether ElderShield should be made mandatory for every Singaporean.

sections.label: Palliative care costs and MediSave
sections.summary: Home palliative care lasts about two months; most hospice patients pay nothing out-of-pocket, and MOH will extend the $2,500 MediSave limit to day hospice.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: For home palliative care, the median care period is around two months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: And in terms of affordability, for inpatient hospice, eight in 10 patients have zero out-of-pocket payments and for home palliative patients, nine in 10 did not have to make out-of-pocket payments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Later this year, MOH will further enhance financial support for palliative care by extending the $2,500 MediSave lifetime withdrawal limit for home palliative care to include day hospice services.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Similar to home palliative patients, day hospice patients diagnosed with terminal cancer or end-stage organ failure will not be subject to this withdrawal limit if the claim is made from the patient's own MediSave account.

sections.label: IP premium components
sections.summary: IP premiums have a MediShield Life component for basic subsidised care and an additional private insurance component.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: IP premiums have two components: there is a MediShield Life component, which is sufficient for basic, subsidised healthcare services, and there is an additional private insurance component.

sections.label: MediSave limits for private insurance
sections.summary: MediSave fully pays MediShield Life premiums, but a limit is set for private insurance so Singaporeans keep enough MediSave for old age.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Mr Pritam Singh also asked to increase the MediSave Additional Withdrawal Limits, or AWLs, to be sufficient for Standard IP premiums at all ages.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: MediShield Life premiums can be fully paid for by MediSave.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Singaporeans who wish to purchase private insurance can use their MediSave to pay for the additional private insurance component, up to the AWL.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We need to set a limit for the use of MediSave for private insurance, including the Standard IP, so that Singaporeans will have sufficient MediSave balances to support their healthcare needs when they grow old.

sections.label: Pharmaceuticals under Health Products Act
sections.summary: Pharmaceutical products will be ported to the Health Products Act and regulated as therapeutic products, alongside medical devices and cosmetics.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Pharmaceutical products will be ported over to the Health Products Act to be regulated under the Health Products Act as therapeutic products, in addition to the medical devices and cosmetic products that are already under the Health Products Act.

sections.label: Therapeutic products review and outbreak measures
sections.summary: Feedback was supportive; MOH hopes to finalise the review and bring therapeutic products into the Health Products Act by year end, with contingency requirements for outbreaks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: The feedback has been supportive and we hope to be able to finalise the review shortly and to bring over the therapeutic products into the Health Products Act by the end of this year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Having said that, MOH does build in contingency requirements into our service contracts to respond to health emergencies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: And in the event of a disease outbreak, MOH will reprioritise our budget to ensure that we are able to implement all these control measures.

sections.label: TAF programme and Holistic Health Framework
sections.summary: The TAF programme ran from 1992 to 2007, cut obesity from 14% to about 9.8% in 2002, drew stigma feedback, and was replaced by the Holistic Health Framework.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: On the issue of the TAF programme, it was implemented in 1992 and discontinued in 2007.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: The objective of the TAF programme is to enable all our overweight and obese students to achieve a healthy weight and while it showed success in reducing obesity rate from 14% to about 9.8% in 2002, MOE did receive quite a number of feedback, both from parents as well as students, that some of the students felt stigmatised by this programme.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Since it was discontinued in 2007, MOE replaced it with a different programme called the Holistic Health Framework (HHF) which is a more holistic approach towards health, rather than just focusing on weight alone.

sections.label: Zika three-pronged approach
sections.summary: MOH adopts a three-pronged approach for Zika, as for any emerging disease, mentioned in the reply.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: For the second one on Zika, just like any emerging diseases, including Zika, MOH adopts a three-pronged approach which I have mentioned in my reply.

sections.label: Portable medical benefits work
sections.summary: The speaker worked with unions and employers' group on portable medical benefits at MOM and continues at MOH.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: Please keep replies short and succinct as well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: I had been working with the unions and the employers' group when I was in the Ministry of Manpower, to look at the portable medical benefits, and I continue to do so after I have moved over to MOH.

sections.label: Tax incentives and My Health Hub
sections.summary: Tax incentives allow up to 2% deductions for portable medical benefits, and My Health Hub draws personal health records from birth to end of life.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: These are possibilities, and we do have tax incentives for them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: They can claim up to 2% tax deductions for the cost of the portable medical benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: On the health records from birth to school, adult and retirement, we have introduced an app called "My Health Hub" which draws data from your personal health records, including your screening and vaccination records from birth to the end of life.

sections.label: Chronic disease withdrawal limit
sections.summary: There is a withdrawal limit of $400 per person for management of chronic diseases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Today, we have a withdrawal limit of $400 per person for management of chronic diseases.

sections.label: Considering publishing wait times
sections.summary: The speaker will consider Mr Leon Perera's suggestion to enhance indicators and publish wait times for appointments and walk-ins.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Usually, I try not to reject ideas and suggestions, so we will consider Mr Leon Perera's suggestion carefully and see whether we could enhance our indicators and publish the wait times for both appointments and walk-ins.

sections.label: Family Medicine Clinics pilot
sections.summary: Polyclinics and private GPs should work together, and six or seven pilot Family Medicine Clinics exist with hopes to expand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: In primary care, polyclinics and private GPs should work together.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We have also introduced Family Medicine Clinics which are still in the pilot phase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We have six or seven of them and we hope to expand and have more.

sections.label: Training own doctors
sections.summary: The priority is to train Singapore's own doctors and give them specialist training opportunities if able.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Our priority is to train our own doctors, to provide them with opportunities to go into specialist training if they are able to.

sections.label: Withdrawing amendment, Dr Chia
sections.summary: Dr Chia Shi-Lu is asked whether he wishes to withdraw his amendment, and he begs leave to withdraw it.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: Do you wish to withdraw your amendment, Dr Chia Shi-Lu?

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
sentences.text: I am certain the feedback and suggestions will be useful as we work to strengthen our healthcare system.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
sentences.text: I would be very happy to proffer them all a cup of teh-O kosong or kopi-O kosong for all their efforts!

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
sentences.text: So, Mdm Chair, I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.
